ECE 6390 / RF links

Noise cascade

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows why early receiver stages have disproportionate influence on input-referred noise.

For matched cascaded stages, Friis' noise formula is Ftotal = F₁ + (F₂ − 1)/G₁ + (F₃ − 1)/(G₁G₂). Noise factors F and power gains G in this sum are linear quantities.

An early low-noise gain makes later stages' input-referred noise contributions smaller. A passive loss L at the reference temperature has gain 1/L and noise factor L, so placing it first carries a substantial noise penalty.

Equivalent input noise temperature is Te = (Ftotal − 1)T₀. A front filter can still serve an important overload or interference role; the small-signal noise calculation evaluates a different constraint.

Example

For a loss L = 2 and an amplifier with F = 2, G = 100, loss first gives Ftotal = 4. Amplifier first gives Ftotal = 2.01, assuming the common reference-temperature model.

    Practice

    1. Why is it incorrect to insert a 20 dB gain directly as G₁ = 20 in Friis' linear noise sum?

    Convert a power gain from decibels to a ratio first.

    A 20 dB power gain is 10² = 100. Using 20 would divide later noise by the wrong gain and overestimate its contribution.
